papers.title: FEM-guided feedforward control based on melt pool depth for geometry-dependent thermal management in Ti-6Al-4V laser-wire DED
papers.first_author_affiliation: Korea Additive Manufacturing Innovation Center, Korea Institute of Industrial Technology, Siheung, Republic of Korea

corresponding_authors.name: Hyub Lee
corresponding_authors.affiliation: Korea Additive Manufacturing Innovation Center, Korea Institute of Industrial Technology, Siheung, Republic of Korea

concepts: Thermal management of electronic devices and systems

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文虽然关注Ti-6Al-4V的增材制造过程控制，但未涉及力学或疲劳性能，仅间接相关。
llm.why_not_core: The paper does not present any experimental or computational mechanical/fatigue characterization of Ti-6Al-4V; its focus is on melt pool depth control and thermal management, not on strength, ductility, fatigue life, or other mechanical properties.

summary_zh.motivation: 为解决激光-丝材直接能量沉积过程中几何形状引起的热积累问题，提出基于熔池深度的前馈控制方法。
summary_zh.method: 利用有限元仿真建立熔池深度与工艺参数的关系，结合实时监测实现前馈控制。
summary_zh.result: 该方法能够有效减少结构不同位置的热变化，提高成形均匀性。
summary_zh.validation: 通过变壁厚薄壁结构的实验验证了控制方法的有效性。

summary_en.motivation: To address geometry-induced heat accumulation in laser-wire DED of Ti-6Al-4V, this paper proposes a feedforward control strategy based on melt pool depth.
summary_en.method: A FEM model is used to relate melt pool depth to process parameters, enabling real-time feedforward control.
summary_en.result: The approach significantly reduces thermal variation across the build, improving process stability.
summary_en.validation: Experimental validation on a thin-wall structure with variable thickness demonstrates the effectiveness of the control scheme.
